The Oxford Shakespeare

My mistress’ eyes are nothing like the sun / Coral is far more red than her lips’ red: / If snow be white, why then her breasts are dun; / If hairs be wires, black wires grow on her head… / And yet, by heaven, I think my love as rare / As any she belied with false compare.—
Sonnet CXXX

William

Shakespeare

The Oxford Shakespeare

Edited by W. J. Craig

The 1914 Oxford edition of the 
Complete Works of William Shakespeare
 ranks among the most authoritative published in the twentieth century. The 37 plays, 154 sonnets and miscellaneous verse constitute the literary cornerstone of Western civilization.
